quotes.text:
AI is shaping the future whether we like it or not.

Technology itself is not the problem. The problem is deploying powerful tools without guardrails, transparency, or accountability.

AI should be a tool that works for people – not one that extracts value and burdens workers. https://t.co/KHUjnt3Brv

This term is sometimes used to tell a story about automation as both a future that we cannot escape and a race that we must win at all costs. But underneath this story is a very small number of powerful companies with access to massive amounts of data and computing resources. And the lesson we are supposed to learn is almost always the same: that government must stay out of the way and keep its hands off AI.

The data centers that power AI and other technologies consume enormous amounts of energy, which can strain aging infrastructure, drive up electricity bills, and have adverse effects on the environment. Our constituents deserve greater transparency and accountability about resource use, community benefit agreements that ensure residents share in economic gains, and a real seat at the table as AI development expands.

If AI is going to reshape our economy in the coming years, then we need to make sure that workers and communities truly benefit from, and not just bear the costs of, this technology boom. Because when we unleash technology without guardrails, workers will always pay the price.

Today marks the seventh hearing this Committee has held on artificial intelligence (AI) this Congress. [...] And is this singular focus even amounting to anything? After seven AI hearings, Committee Republicans have not produced a single plan or bill to protect workers from AI risks.

Additionally, some states have stepped up to protect workers by passing their own guardrails on the use of AI. But instead of holding tech companies accountable, the Trump Administration is actively undermining these states’ AI laws and looking to pass legislation to preempt any regulation.

If we are going to uplift working Americans, a bold pro-worker AI agenda must help more workers join unions, place appropriate limits on AI, safeguard worker privacy, and enforce worker protections. [...] At the end of the day, AI is a tool. Whether this tool will benefit corporations and their wealthy executives or the working class and the middle class is a policy choice.

I introduced 9 amendments to the NDAA. 

The amendments aim to center human rights in the military and foreign policy; strengthen oversight over the DoD’s use of AI; support Sudanese civil society; and hold governments engaged in transnational repression accountable. https://t.co/ELuStNc2JD

Proud to support @FrancescaHongWI for Wisconsin Governor.

Medicare for All.
Universal childcare.
No corporate PAC money.
Moratorium on AI data centers.

This is the future Wisconsin deserves—a state where every single resident can thrive. https://t.co/RnuCB6Z7Zx
I mean, I've got kids. I don't want my kids around robots. That feels a little creepy.

Any time an industry comes to you and says, “Help us regulate ourselves,” you have to be skeptical.

AI needs strong guardrails to protect the public—not rules written to make tech CEOs and billionaires even richer. https://t.co/R0Btj8VdqN

Flock cameras track your every move. It’s creepy, dangerous, and raises serious civil rights concerns.

Big Tech is pushing us toward an AI surveillance state. Americans deserve privacy, not unchecked surveillance.

Ban Flock NOW.
